quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #16
										  					
  

33 Questions • Passing Score 27

questions.question: Regulatory signs are usually ____ and must always be obeyed.

options.text: White
Blue
Green
Orange

questions.correctAnswerText: White
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs control traffic movement. They are white with black markings. Drivers must always obey them.

questions.question: After stopping for a school bus that is unloading children:

options.text: Do not proceed until the children wave to you.
Watch for children walking along the side of the road.
Accelerate quickly.
Turn on your emergency flashers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Watch for children walking along the side of the road.
questions.explanation: After stopping for a school bus, watch for children walking along the side of the road. Always drive carefully near children.

questions.question: Stress can affect your driving by:

options.text: Lowering your ability to focus on driving.
Decreasing your chances of an accident.
Causing you to fall asleep at the wheel.
Making you more aware of others around you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Lowering your ability to focus on driving.
questions.explanation: Stress and strong emotions can hurt your driving ability. Worry, anger, fear, or sadness can reduce your focus on the road. It is better to wait and drive when you feel calm.

questions.question: What should you do if your vehicle's right wheels leave the pavement?

options.text: Stop quickly.
Immediately pull all the way off of the road and get back on when it is safe.
Accelerate and steer back on the road quickly.
Take your foot off the accelerator, slow down, then ease back onto the road when it is safe to do so.

questions.correctAnswerText: Take your foot off the accelerator, slow down, then ease back onto the road when it is safe to do so.
questions.explanation: Don't panic if your right wheels leave the pavement. Take your foot off the gas and steer parallel to the road. Slow down and gently steer back onto the road. Keep both hands on the wheel and check for traffic before returning to the pavement.

questions.question: When approached by an emergency vehicle using its siren and/or flashing lights, you must immediately:

options.text: Pull to the right and stop.
Pull to the right and slow down.
Pull to the right and turn on your four-way flashers.
Stop and let the emergency vehicle pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull to the right and stop.
questions.explanation: When you see an emergency vehicle with lights and/or sirens coming, pull to the right side of the road and stop right away.

questions.question: When encountering a funeral procession, a driver:

options.text: May not drive between the vehicles forming the procession unless authorized to do so by a police officer.
May not enter an intersection and cross the path of a funeral procession as it is proceeding through a solid red traffic light.
Must yield the right-of-way to any motor vehicle that is part of the funeral procession.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: State law requires drivers and pedestrians to yield to funeral processions. You cannot drive between procession vehicles unless a police officer tells you to. You cannot enter an intersection while a funeral procession is passing through.

questions.question: Hydroplaning is usually caused by:

options.text: Excessive stops.
Sudden stops.
Sudden turns.
Excessive speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Excessive speed.
questions.explanation: As you drive faster, your tires lose their ability to clear water from the road. If you go too fast, your tires may lose grip completely, causing your vehicle to slide on water. This is hydroplaning.

questions.question: When may you proceed through an intersection with a stop sign but no stop line or crosswalk?

options.text: After slowing down to verify that there is no cross traffic
After coming to a complete stop and verifying that it is safe to proceed
After you have stopped at least 20 feet prior to the intersection
After slowing down to a speed of 10 mph

questions.correctAnswerText: After coming to a complete stop and verifying that it is safe to proceed
questions.explanation: Stop completely before the stop line or crosswalk at intersections with stop signs. If there is no stop line or crosswalk, stop before entering the intersection. Proceed only when it is safe.

questions.question: Increase your following distance when:

options.text: Driving behind a large vehicle that blocks your vision.
Exiting an expressway.
Following a motorcycle.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Increase your following distance when behind a large vehicle blocking your view, in bad weather, in heavy traffic, when exiting an expressway, when behind a motorcycle or bicycle, or when someone is tailgating you.

questions.question: Which of the following influence(s) the effects of alcohol?

options.text: The amount of food in the stomach
The body weight of an individual
How much time passes between drinks
All three choices

questions.correctAnswerText: All three choices
questions.explanation: Your blood alcohol content depends on how much you drink, how much time passes between drinks, and your weight. Food slows alcohol absorption but cannot prevent intoxication from drinking too much.

questions.question: You are driving on a narrow road and meet an oncoming vehicle. You must:

options.text: Pull completely off the road and stop.
Give the oncoming vehicle at least half of the road's main traveled area.
Demand that the other vehicle pull over.
Turn on your high beam headlights so the other driver sees you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Give the oncoming vehicle at least half of the road's main traveled area.
questions.explanation: On narrow roads, you must give oncoming vehicles at least half of the main traveled area. Both drivers need adequate space to pass each other safely.

questions.question: Roads become very slippery:

options.text: When it has been raining for one hour or more.
The day after it rains.
During the first 10 to 15 minutes of a rainstorm.
Right after the rain stops.

questions.correctAnswerText: During the first 10 to 15 minutes of a rainstorm.
questions.explanation: Roads become very slippery in the first 10 to 15 minutes of rain. The rain brings oil from the asphalt to the road surface. In hot weather, this is worse because heat causes more oil to rise.

questions.question: When changing lanes you should not:

options.text: Check your side and rearview mirrors.
Use your turn signal to show your intention.
Check for other drivers moving into your lane.
Use your cell phone to call the police about road conditions ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your cell phone to call the police about road conditions ahead.
questions.explanation: Before changing lanes, check your mirrors for traffic behind you. Use your turn signal to tell other drivers you plan to change lanes. Look for other drivers who might be moving into the same lane.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: Narrow bridge ahead.
A lane is ending or the road is narrowing ahead.
Industrial area.
Freeway on-ramp ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: A lane is ending or the road is narrowing ahead.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are diamond-shaped with black markings on a yellow background. They warn drivers of upcoming hazards. This sign warns that the right lane is ending or the road is getting narrower.

questions.question: When a driver behind you wants to pass, you should:

options.text: Speed up.
Keep the same speed.
Slow down to give the other driver room to pass safely and quickly.
Change lanes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down to give the other driver room to pass safely and quickly.
questions.explanation: When a driver behind you wants to pass, slow down. This gives them enough space in front of your vehicle to complete the pass safely and in less time.

questions.question: A good defensive driver:

options.text: Always drives slowly.
Watches what other drivers are doing.
Drives at a constant speed.
Only drives in familiar areas.

questions.correctAnswerText: Watches what other drivers are doing.
questions.explanation: Any driver can become distracted. A defensive driver watches what other drivers are doing and expects problems before they happen.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: Trucks only.
Trucks are entering the highway.
A steep hill is coming.
Trucks have the right-of-way.

questions.correctAnswerText: A steep hill is coming.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are diamond-shaped with black markings on a yellow background. They warn drivers of upcoming hazards. This sign tells drivers that a steep hill is ahead and they should adjust their speed to drive safely.

questions.question: You are stopped in a line of vehicles at a stop sign. After the vehicles ahead pass through and there is no cross traffic, you:

options.text: May go through without stopping again.
Must stop at the stop sign before going through.
May slowly roll past the stop sign.
May follow the vehicle in front of you without stopping.

questions.correctAnswerText: Must stop at the stop sign before going through.
questions.explanation: You must always make a complete stop at the stop sign and check for traffic before proceeding. Do not feel rushed by other vehicles to skip this safety step.

questions.question: Emergency vehicles:

options.text: Have the right-of-way when using sirens, horns, and flashing lights.
May use a loudspeaker to give instructions.
May follow each other.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: You must give the right-of-way to police cars, fire engines, ambulances, and other emergency vehicles using a siren or air horn and a red or blue flashing light. Follow any instructions given over their loudspeakers. Emergency vehicles often follow each other, so only proceed when you are sure the way is clear.

questions.question: Which of the following must you obey over the other three?

options.text: A steady red light
A police officer
A stop sign
A flashing red light

questions.correctAnswerText: A police officer
questions.explanation: Orders from a police officer come before signs, signals, and road markings. Police officers, fire police, road work zone flag persons, and school crossing guards are all authorized to direct traffic.

questions.question: What should you do when driving in foggy weather?

options.text: Turn on your low beam headlights.
Turn on your hazard lights.
It is okay to drive at the maximum speed limit.
Do not drive faster than 10 miles per hour.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn on your low beam headlights.
questions.explanation: You must use your headlights when you cannot see 500 feet ahead. Use low beams, not high beams. High beams reflect light back at you in fog or rain, making it harder to see.

questions.question: An emergency vehicle with flashing lights approaches you on a one-way street. What must you do?

options.text: Drive with your hazard lights on.
Move to the side of the road and stop.
Speed up and take the nearest exit.
Slow down until the vehicle passes you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to the side of the road and stop.
questions.explanation: When an emergency vehicle with flashing lights or a siren approaches, move to the nearest roadside and stop.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: One-way road.
No right turn.
Exit.
Sharp right turn ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Sharp right turn ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that there is a sharp right turn ahead.

questions.question: Which statement is true about passing other vehicles?

options.text: Signal at least 100 feet before changing lanes to pass and check for oncoming traffic.
Check your mirrors and look over your left shoulder to see your blind spot when passing.
Wait until you see both headlights of the passed car in your rearview mirror before moving back to your lane.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: When passing, signal at least 100 feet ahead. Check your mirrors and blind spot. Wait until you see both headlights of the other car in your rearview mirror before returning to your lane.

questions.question: How can you help prevent rear-end collisions?

options.text: Avoid sudden stops.
Check your mirrors and blind spots before stopping.
Release the gas pedal to slow down before applying the brakes.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Sudden stops make it hard for drivers behind you to stop in time. Release the gas pedal first to slow down, then press the brake pedal smoothly. This gives drivers behind you more time to react.

questions.question: What is the safe way to pass a bicycle?

options.text: Honk to let the bicyclist know you are passing.
Drive in the bicycle lane to get around them.
Slow down and give them as much space as possible.
Speed ahead to get in front of the bicyclist.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and give them as much space as possible.
questions.explanation: Slow down and give bicyclists plenty of space. Bicyclists have less protection than drivers. Passing too quickly can cause them to lose control.

questions.question: When passing a large vehicle, drivers of small vehicles should be prepared for:

options.text: Loud noises.
Excess air pollution.
Strong wind gusts from the large vehicle.
Falling vehicle parts.

questions.correctAnswerText: Strong wind gusts from the large vehicle.
questions.explanation: Large vehicles create strong wind gusts that can push smaller vehicles off course. Be ready to steer carefully when passing large vehicles at high speeds.

questions.question: How can you prevent drowsiness on long trips?

options.text: Turn on your car radio.
Slow down.
Stop regularly to rest and stretch.
Move your eyes side to side as you drive.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop regularly to rest and stretch.
questions.explanation: Take regular breaks on long trips. Stop to rest and stretch, even if you do not feel tired.

questions.question: When a police officer is directing traffic at a working traffic light, what should drivers do?

options.text: Follow the traffic light.
Follow the officer's directions.
Honk at the officer.
Watch what other cars are doing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Follow the officer's directions.
questions.explanation: Traffic lights control traffic at intersections. However, when a police officer is directing traffic, follow the officer's directions instead of the traffic light.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Slow down or stop.
Stop if necessary.
You must come to a complete stop.
Drive with caution and be ready to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must come to a complete stop.
questions.explanation: An eight-sided sign means stop. You must come to a complete stop and wait for vehicles and pedestrians to clear before you go.

questions.question: You are approaching a railroad crossing and do not see or hear a train. When must you stop?

options.text: If a stop sign is posted.
If a crossing gate is lowered.
If the crossing lights are flashing.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Always stop before railroad tracks if you see flashing red lights, a lowered crossing gate, a stop sign, a flagger's signal, or a train. If you are unsure whether a train is close enough to be unsafe, stop. Never try to cross ahead of a train.

questions.question: What does a steady green light at an intersection mean?

options.text: You must slow down and prepare to stop.
You must stop and check for oncoming traffic before proceeding.
You may drive through if the road is clear.
You may not turn right.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may drive through if the road is clear.
questions.explanation: A steady green light means you can drive through the intersection if the road is clear. You can also turn right or left unless a sign says you cannot. When turning, yield to other vehicles and pedestrians in the intersection.

questions.question: Why is a leaky exhaust system dangerous?

options.text: It causes hearing loss.
It causes pollution.
It can cause carbon monoxide poisoning.
It causes poor engine performance.

questions.correctAnswerText: It can cause carbon monoxide poisoning.
questions.explanation: The exhaust system removes exhaust gases and keeps fumes out of the passenger compartment. A leak allows carbon monoxide to enter the vehicle. Fix leaks right away to prevent poisoning.
